title: Quantification of Nitrogen and Phosphorus in grass and soil samples using ICP-OES
author: Gabriel Mayengo

steps_raw.instruction: We have made the observation that soil and grass samples from nutrient hotspots and controls are not the same. We have come up with the following hypothesis: Nutrient contents ie Nitrogen (N) and Phosphorus (P) in nutrient hotspots ie termite mounds and grazing lawns is higher than their surroundings.

A total of 101 grass samples collected from 10 termite mounds, 10 non termite mounds (controls), 6 grazing lawns, 6 non grazing lawns (controls), 30 pots containing and fertilizing experiment plots. Further we had a total of 24 soil samples collected from hotspot and non-hotspot areas.

Total nitrogen was determined by dry combustion (elementary analysis) using an elemental analyser (Vario EL, Elementar, Germany; ISO 13878
Soil quality - Determination of total nitrogen content by dry combustion ("elemental analysis").

2.1) plant samples:
Pressure digestion with nitric acid in quartz vessels (200 mg sample/
5 ml nitric acid, 220°C, 100 bar, 20 minutes) in a microwave-heated
high pressure digestion system (Ultra Clave II, MLS GmbH, Germany).

2.2) Total P content soil samples:
The sample (3 g) was weighed into a quartz digestion tube and a mixture
(aqua regia) of HCl (37%) and HNO3 (65%) is added. After standing over
night at room temperature the sample was boiled for two hours under
reflux conditions, cooled, transferred to a 100-ml volumetric flask,
filled up with water and then filtered into a storage vessel.
Soil quality - Extraction of trace elements soluble in aqua regia (ISO 11466)

Measuring of total P content in both soil and plant samples:
Elements was measured by ICP-OES (inductively coupled plasma optical
emission spectrometry) using an agilent instrument and external
calibration against certified standards (various suppliers).

Water quality - Determination of selected elements by inductively
coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) (ISO 11885)
Grass and soil samples collected from controls were used as controls.

A Generalized Linear Mixed Model was further used to evaluate the effect of nutrient hotspots site i.e. hotspot vs control and their distance i.e. closeness to the nutrient hotspot and their interaction with nutrient content (N). Grass and soil samples from hotspots vs controls were compared using one-way ANOVA. In the fertilizing experiment, grass N and P content levels were measured before setting the experiment and after application of fertilizer, then compared across treatments using a one-way ANOVA. Further, for pot experiment, grass samples across the plots were compared using one-way ANOVA. Box plots were used to plot the results. A t-test will be performed to determine if the case group differs from the control group. If the case group produces more nutrient levels ie N, P than the control, we can then conclude that nutrient level has impact on grass appearance and is among important cue in attracting ungulates ie grazers to graze around them.
